papers.title: Novel dissolving microneedles incorporating natural carrier-free self-assembled nanoparticles synergized with electroacupuncture for diabetic wound healing.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zeng Y, Zeng H, Huo H, Zeng M, Li M et al.
papers.abstract: Diabetic wounds (DW) are one of the most common complications of diabetes with complex pathogenesis, causing high morbidity and disability. Conventional therapies fail to resolve multiple obstacles to DW healing, urgently requiring efficient and safe novel interventions. Compounds from medicine and food homology substances have attracted widespread attention owing to their superior biosafety and diverse pharmacological activities. Herein, carrier-free APC and GQS nanoparticles were manufactured separately via self-assembly using medicine and food homology bioactive components, including astragalus polysaccharide, chlorogenic acid, quercetin, β-sitosterol, and glycyrrhizin acid. Subsequently, dissolvable APC@GQS@MNs co-loaded with APC and GQS were constructed using polyvinylpyrrolidone, hyaluronic acid, and aloe vera as matrix materials. Physicochemical characterization confirmed that APC@GQS@MNs have a well-defined conical morphology, satisfactory mechanical strength, and favorable skin penetration. The APC@GQS@MNs also enabled efficient selective scavenging of cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS), while physiological ROS were less affected. Meanwhile, APC@GQS@MNs exhibited favorable biocompatibility, reduced intracellular ROS levels, ameliorated oxidative stress-induced damage to cell proliferation, migration and tube formation, promoted M1 to M2 macrophage polarization, and effectively inhibited the growth and biofilm formation of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. In vivo results showed that APC@GQS@MNs promoted collagen deposition, re-epithelialization, and reduced local inflammatory infiltration in DW by upregulating CD31, CD163, IL-10 and suppressing iNOS, NF-κB, and TNF-α signaling. Notably, APC@GQS@MNs combined with electroacupuncture exerted synergistic effects, which further ameliorated the wound microenvironment and markedly accelerated wound healing and tissue regeneration. Such synergistic therapy modulates local wound states and inflammatory responses, laying a promising foundation for the management of DW.

papers.title: A GelMA hydrogel co-loaded with ursolic acid, ferulic acid and naringin facilitates dentin regeneration by providing a multi-component odontogenic microenvironment.
papers.authors: Che J, Yang A, Mo F, Gao Y, Li Y, Cui Y et al.
papers.abstract: Dental caries is a prevalent bacterial infectious disease, yet current clinical treatments remain limited because conventional restorative materials provide only mechanical filling and fail to induce dental tissue regeneration. Herein, we developed a composite gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel system (Gel/UFN) co-loaded with three active components from traditional Chinese medicine, including ursolic acid (UA), ferulic acid (FA) and naringin (Nar), to remodel the carious microenvironment and promote dentin remineralization and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation. Gel/UFN showed excellent biocompatibility and favorable physicochemical and mechanical properties for dental applications, supporting adhesion and proliferation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). Functionally, Gel/UFN significantly inhibited Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) growth and biofilm formation, downregulated inflammatory cytokine expression and promoted the migration and angiogenesis of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). More importantly, Gel/UFN upregulated odontogenesis-related genes in hDPSCs, thereby enhancing odontogenic differentiation, alkaline phosphatase activity, collagen maturation and regenerative mineralization. In vivo, Gel/UFN exhibited slow degradation and sustained drug release for over 55 days. After implantation of Gel/UFN-filled dentin discs into nude mice, H&E staining demonstrated the formation of vascular structures, dentin-like mineralized tissue and cell-rich pulp-like tissue. Western blot analysis further revealed increased expression of the odontogenesis-related proteins RUNX2, DSPP, DMP1, and COL1A1 in the Gel/UFN group, providing additional protein-level evidence of its pro-odontogenic effects in vivo. These newly formed tissues were observed to cover exposed dentinal tubules on the surface of dentin disc using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Micro-CT further confirmed that dental tissue induced by Gel/UFN exhibited a higher remineralization density at the defect site, supporting enhanced dentin remineralization. Overall, Gel/UFN may serve as a promising bioactive hydrogel platform for dentin repair and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation through antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic and pro-differentiation effects.

papers.title: Effect of Kunxian capsule, a novel Tripterygium wilfordii preparation, on reducing proteinuria and slowing renal function decline in diabetic kidney disease: a 48-week randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Chen S, Gao Y, Liang Z, Zhang Y, Wang C, Tang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a leading cause of chronic kidney disease, remains a clinical challenge despite renin-angiotensin system blockade. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan in patients with DKD.
Eighty patients with DKD were randomly assigned to either the experimental group (standard therapy with irbesartan plus Kunxian capsule) or the control group (standard therapy with irbesartan) for 48 weeks. Primary outcomes included the proteinuria remission rate, degree of proteinuria reduction, and median time to remission. Secondary outcomes included the slope of eGFR decline and the incidence of renal composite hard endpoint. Safety was assessed by monitoring adverse events. This trial was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov on March 2, 2021 (No. NCT04981613).
In the intention-to-treat analysis, the experimental group had a higher proteinuria remission rate (57.50% vs. 25.00%), a shorter median time to remission (5 months vs. not reached), and a greater reduction in 24-hour urinary protein than the control group. A lower incidence of renal composite hard endpoint was observed in the experimental group (10.00% vs. 32.50%), accompanied by a slower eGFR decline. No significant differences in the incidence of adverse events were observed between the two groups. Inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, were significantly reduced in the experimental group.
Adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan improved the proteinuria remission rate and attenuated renal function decline in patients with DKD, supporting its potential as a promising adjunctive therapy.

papers.title: Neuropharmacological effects of Salvia officinalis: molecular mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and clinical potential.
papers.authors: Sabet AZ, Ahmadnia H, Shahsavari K, Khanavi M, Esfahani HM, Yazarlu O et al.
papers.abstract: Salvia officinalis (sage), a cornerstone of traditional medicine, has attracted significant scientific interest for its neuroprotective benefits. This review synthesizes evidence on the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying its potential therapeutic efficacy, which are attributed to bioactive compounds including phenolic acids (rosmarinic and caffeic acid), flavonoids, and terpenoids. Six key mechanisms have been identified. First, S. officinalis enhances cholinergic activity by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, directly counteracting cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease. Second, it exerts significant antioxidant effects by neutralizing free radicals, upregulating catalase and superoxide dismutase, and reducing lipid peroxidation. Third, anti-inflammatory actions involve suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) and inhibiting COX-2/PGE2 pathways. Fourth, S. officinalis modulates neurotrophic factors, upregulating BDNF and GDNF to support neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity. Fifth, it interacts with neurotransmitter systems-activating opioid receptors for analgesia, enhancing GABAergic activity for anxiolytic and anticonvulsant effects, and influencing serotonergic and adrenergic pathways for mood regulation. Sixth, it may reduce amyloid-beta aggregation and reduces tau hyperphosphorylation. Additionally, phytoestrogenic components may contribute to benefits against cognitive decline and mood disorders during menopause. By integrating findings from in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies, this review provides a comprehensive overview of S. officinalis as a promising multi-target therapeutic agent for neurological and neuropsychiatric conditions, highlighting its potential as a natural alternative or complement to conventional pharmacotherapies in managing complex brain disorders.

papers.title: Characteristic Dihydrophenanthrenes from Spiranthes sinensis with Therapeutic Potential for Ischemic Stroke.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
papers.authors: Qi J, Xu L, Wang Y, Li L, Zhang G, Liu X et al.
papers.abstract: Spiranthes sinensis, known as "Panlongshen", is an edible traditional Chinese medicine, widely used in herbal teas and health-promoting foods. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective properties of S. sinensis against ischemic stroke for the first time. Bioactivity-guided isolation yielded 19 dihydrophenanthrenes, including 9 undescribed compounds (7a/7b, 9-11, 12a/12b-13a/13b). These dihydrophenanthrenes demonstrated significant antineuroinflammatory activity against NO production in LPS-induced BV-2 microglia cells, with IC50 values ranging from 1.5 to 34.8 μM, which were greater than that of the positive drug (minocycline, IC50: 34.9 μM). Furthermore, coelonin (2) reduced inflammatory cytokines in BV-2 microglia and preserved PC12 cells' viability under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Mechanistic investigations revealed that coelonin (2) exerts its antineuroinflammatory effects by targeting MAP3K7 and suppressing the NF-κB signaling cascade. In vivo, coelonin alleviated ischemic-reperfusion injury after MCAO. These findings revealed the neuroprotective and anti-ischemic stroke effects of S. sinensis and identified dihydrophenanthrenes as its key active constituents.

papers.title: Acupuncture for Cardiovascular Diseases: A Review of Clinical Efficacy, Mechanisms, and Translational Perspectives.
papers.authors: Shao Y, Li Z, Zhang J, Dou W, Lu Y, Liu B et al.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality and disability, imposing a profound societal burden. While conventional pharmacotherapy and surgical interventions are foundational, they are frequently limited by adverse effects, postoperative complications, and suboptimal long-term prognoses. Acupuncture and electroacupuncture (EA), core components of traditional Chinese medicine, have attracted growing attention as low-risk, non-invasive, neuromodulatory therapies. A growing body of clinical data suggests that acupuncture/EA may be beneficial in managing diverse CVDs, including coronary heart disease, hypertension, arrhythmias, heart failure, and myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury. Furthermore, mechanistic investigations have expanded into modern interdisciplinary fields, revealing complex regulatory networks involving central neuromodulation, intracellular signaling, cytoprotection, and the gut microbiota. This narrative review synthesizes the core clinical evidence and underlying mechanisms of acupuncture/EA in cardiovascular care. We additionally collate standardized clinical protocols, encompassing core acupoints and stimulation parameters. Finally, this paper critically examines current research limitations and outlines future translational trajectories, aiming to provide a comprehensive reference for integrating acupuncture/EA into standardized CVD prevention and treatment research.

papers.title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy for Determination of Paeoniflorin in Paeoniae Radix Rubra of Tongtian Oral Liquid.
papers.authors: Hongliang L, Xiaoqing Z, Taiyong A, Jun W, Xinyu L, Siqi C et al.
papers.abstract: Considering the limitations of conventional high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), including lengthy analysis times and high costs, near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with chemometrics was investigated as a rapid method for determining paeoniflorin in the Paeoniae Radix Rubra extract of Tongtian Oral Liquid. Three samples were acquired from each of 67 independent production batches. Each sample was measured three times by NIR spectroscopy, and the three technical measurements were averaged wavelength-by-wavelength, yielding 201 representative spectra for modeling. The paeoniflorin concentration ranged from 2.3 to 50.0 mg/mL, and spectra were collected over 908.1-1676.2 nm. Following a three-way spectrum-level split into training, validation, and test sets, 87 wavelengths with Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) > 1.0 were selected using Partial Least Squares-Variable Importance in Projection (PLS-VIP). Among seven chemometric algorithms, Lasso regression achieved the best predictive performance (test R2 = 0.9994, Root mean Square error = 1.11 mg/mL, Mean absolute error = 0.89 mg/mL, Residual Predictive Deviation = 12.4), while reducing measurement time from 30-40 min to 2-3 min and the estimated cost by 90%. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis identified several informative wavelengths and spectral regions associated with O-H and C-H absorptions. These findings demonstrate the potential of NIR-based chemometric analysis as a rapid and cost-effective approach to assessing paeoniflorin quality in traditional Chinese medicine manufacturing.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 한약 제조 품질관리에서 근적외선-화학계량학이 빠른 성분 평가 도구가 될 가능성이 있으나, 실제 임상 적용 전에는 공정별 재현성과 외부 검증이 필요하다.

papers.title: Standardized Preparation of Ruyi Jinhuang Paste from Herbal Powder and Its Topical Application for Knee Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Qu Z, Gong Z, Guo T, Xiang Z, Tang K, Tan X et al.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common chronic degenerative disease with an extremely high incidence in middle-aged and elderly people, characterized by a long disease course and progressive aggravation. Knee pain, swelling, and dysfunction severely reduce patients' quality of life and constitute the major health problem in this population. Currently, western medical treatments (such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs]) can relieve symptoms. However, long-term use is often accompanied by gastrointestinal and cardiovascular risks, which can hardly meet patients' needs for long-term safe management, and the recurrence rate is relatively high. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has a long history and extensive experience in treating orthopedic diseases. As a characteristic TCM therapy, herbal topical application is a commonly used TCM nursing intervention that can be prepared and applied without complex equipment, making it potentially suitable for use outside the hospital after appropriate instruction. This paper aims to introduce a standardized method for preparing and applying herbal ointment for self-management among KOA patients, including site selection, procedural steps, treatment duration, and other key aspects.

papers.title: Qi Yin San Liang San prevents gefitinib-induced nociceptive hypersensitivity by modulating TRPV1 channel activity.
papers.authors: Yan K, Guo PX, Liang QY, Xu PT, Jin T, Chen LY et al.
papers.abstract:
Qi Yin San Liang San (QYSLS) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used as an adjunctive therapy for malignant tumors, and has been reported to reduce treatment-related toxicities. Gefitinib-associated nociceptive hypersensitivity remains underrecognized, with its underlying causal mechanism poorly defined. It is unclear whether QYSLS can prevent gefitinib-evoked adverse effect and the underlying molecular mechanism remain unknown.
To explore the molecular mechanism of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity and evaluate the preventive effects of QYSLS, with specific investigation of TRPV1 channel activity and CGRP release from dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron under this pathological condition.
A mouse model of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity was established. QYSLS protection was assessed via pain behavioral tests and DRG histopathology. RNA-seq and network pharmacology were used for target screening. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking confirmed direct gefitinib-TRPV1 binding. Calcium imaging evaluated TRPV1 channel activity in primary DRG neurons and TRPV1-overexpressing cells. Trpv1-/- mice were used to validate its function. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining and ELISA measured DRG TRPV1/CGRP expression and CGRP release.
Gefitinib induced time-dependent declines in mechanical withdrawal thresholds (8.7% of the control at day 28) and thermal withdrawal latencies (55.3% of control at day 28), accompanied by DRG injury in mice. DRG RNA-seq revealed elevated Trpv1 transcripts levels and enrichment of ion channel pathways. Gefitinib triggered TRPV1-dependent elevation of intracellular Ca2+ signals in DRG nociceptive neurons. Calcium imaging, SPR, CETSA, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis showed that gefitinib directly activates TRPV1. Residue Y454 is critical for this effect, while it is dispensable for capsaicin-mediated TRPV1 activation, and this activation elicits significant Ca2+ influx, neuronal excitation, and increased CGRP in DRG neurons. Genetic deletion of Trpv1 largely restored pain thresholds and rescued gefitinib-caused neuropathic pain. Oral QYSLS alleviated gefitinib-evoked weight loss, DRG histological damage and nociceptive hypersensitivity (recovered to 50.5% of control for mechanical withdrawal thresholds, and 94.7% of control for thermal withdrawal latency at day 28), accompanied by reductions in gefitinib-triggered DRG TRPV1 and CGRP expression of ∼34.6% and ∼56.1%, respectively. Quercetin and ferulic acid, the key bioactive ingredients of QYSLS, can inhibit gefitinib-induced TRPV1 activation. The analgesic-protective effects of QYSLS were substantially blunted in Trpv1-/- mice.
This work identifies a previously unrecognized mechanism: Gefitinib triggers nociceptive hypersensitivity via DRG TRPV1 direct activation. Residue Y454 is critical for gefitinib- but not capsaicin-evoked TRPV1 activation, and CGRP may act as a downstream effector. QYSLS prevents this nociceptive hypersensitivity largely through TRPV1.

papers.title: Cycloastragenol suppresses LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and promotes M2 polarization via TLR4/NF-κB signaling and SIRT1-related regulation.
papers.authors: Zhou X, Qin S, Guo Y, Niu W, Chang X, Wang S et al.
papers.abstract:
Astragalus has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine for tonifying qi and supporting defensive functions. Cycloastragenol (CAG), a characteristic triterpenoid aglycone derived from Astragalus saponins, has emerging pharmacological relevance in immune and inflammatory regulation, but its role in macrophage inflammatory regulation and phenotypic remodeling remains insufficiently defined.
To investigate the effects of CAG on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophage inflammation and phenotypic remodeling, focusing on Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling and the involvement of sirtuin 1 (SIRT1).
RAW 264.7 macrophages were pretreated with CAG before LPS stimulation. Cytokine secretion, phenotype markers, and inflammatory signaling were evaluated by ELISA, immunofluorescence, reverse transcription quantitative PCR, and Western blotting. SIRT1-targeting small interfering RNA was used for functional evaluation. Network pharmacology prioritized candidate targets, while two acute inflammatory tissue transcriptomes and a normal human immune atlas provided expression context. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations explored candidate CAG-protein interactions.
Compared with LPS alone, CAG at 20 μmol/L reduced TNF-α from 56.15 ± 2.17 to 25.80 ± 1.87 pg/mL and IL-1β from 93.55 ± 2.66 to 44.49 ± 2.85 pg/mL (mean ± standard deviation; both Tukey-adjusted P < 0.0001). At this concentration, CAG decreased inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and CD86 and increased arginase-1 (ARG1) and CD206. Network pharmacology prioritized TLR4 and SIRT1. Wounded human skin and LPS-exposed mouse lungs showed increased expression of the gene encoding monocyte chemoattractant protein-1-induced protein 1 (MCPIP1). The human atlas detected transcripts for these regulators in macrophages and monocytes. CAG attenuated TLR4/NF-κB signaling and partially restored SIRT1 expression. During CAG treatment, SIRT1 silencing increased TLR4 expression, the phosphorylated/total p65 ratio, iNOS, and CD86 and decreased ARG1, weakening the signaling and phenotypic effects of CAG. Docking and simulations suggested possible CAG-protein interactions.
CAG attenuated LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and favored M2-associated phenotypic remodeling, with SIRT1 contributing to these effects. These findings support CAG as a promising Astragalus-derived immunomodulatory candidate and provide a basis for further exploration of its clinical translational potential.

papers.title: Cornus officinalis-derived exosome-like nanovesicles alleviate osteoporosis by attenuating oxidative stress and improving bone homeostasis.
papers.authors: Xi H, Yan S, Liu Y, Huang Y, Gao F, Chen Y et al.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent metabolic bone disorder characterized by impaired bone formation, excessive bone resorption, and progressive microarchitectural deterioration. Oxidative stress and its associated mitochondrial dysfunction are important contributors to osteoblast apoptosis and osteoclast activation. Therefore, developing safe strategies that attenuate oxidative stress and restore bone remodeling balance is of great significance. Cornus officinalis is a traditional herbal medicine with antioxidant and bone-protective potential, providing a promising natural source for osteoporosis intervention. In this study, Cornus officinalis-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (CONVs) were isolated and characterized, and their anti-osteoporotic effects were systematically evaluated. In vitro, CONVs were efficiently internalized by MC3T3-E1 and RAW264.7 cells, showed favorable cytocompatibility, promoted osteogenic differentiation and mineralization, and inhibited osteoclast formation. Under oxidative stress conditions, CONVs reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and attenuated apoptosis in MC3T3-E1 cells. Transcriptomic analysis and molecular validation further suggested that the protective effects of CONVs were associated with restoration of NRF2/HO-1-related antioxidant signaling. In an ovariectomized rat model, oral administration of CONVs improved bone mineral density, trabecular microarchitecture, biomechanical strength, and bone remodeling balance, while showing favorable biosafety. These findings suggest that CONVs may serve as natural nanovesicle-based biomaterials for osteoporosis intervention.

papers.title: Pharmacological agents for promoting diabetic wound healing.
papers.authors: Shang J, Liu Z, Liang M, Ye X, Yin Z, Yang Z et al.
papers.abstract: Diabetic wounds are highly susceptible to chronicity and infection due to impaired healing involving multiple pathophysiological factors. Despite extensive preclinical and clinical research, few approved drugs have been shown to effectively accelerate diabetic wound healing. This review highlights pharmacological interventions for diabetic wound healing, summarizes the current status of drug development, and discusses their potential mechanisms of action. These agents include inflammation-modulating agents, pro-proliferative agents, remodeling-regulating agents, hypoxia- and microcirculation-targeting agents, antioxidant agents, and multi-target agents, such as bioactive constituents from plants and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas. This review aims to guide future drug development strategies for diabetic wound healing.

papers.title: Intradermal thumbtack needling as an adjunctive therapy for sepsis-induced gastrointestinal dysfunction: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of traditional and complementary medicine
papers.authors: Liu T, Ma J, Qiu Y, Xiao Q, Sun Z
papers.abstract:
Sepsis-induced gastrointestinal dysfunction (GID) is common in critically ill patients, leading to impaired motility, feeding intolerance, and poor outcomes. Evidence for acupuncture-related neuromodulation remains limited. Intradermal thumbtack needling (ITN), a minimally invasive technique that provides continuous low-intensity stimulation, may serve as an adjunct in Intensive Care Unit (ICU), but its clinical effects remain unexamined. This study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of ITN in patients with sepsis-induced GID.
Sixty patients with sepsis-induced GID were randomly assigned to the conventional treatment (CT) group or ITN group. Both groups received standard therapies (ventilation, vasopressors, anti-infectives, fluid resuscitation, gastrointestinal mucosal protection, and prokinetics). The ITN group also received ITN at auricular and body acupoints for 7 days. Gastrointestinal function indicators (acute gastrointestinal injury [AGI] grade, gastric antrum motility index [MI], abdominal circumference, intra-abdominal pressure [IAP]), inflammatory markers, and severity scores were assessed before and after treatment. 28-day mortality, ICU length of stay and adverse events were assessed after treatment.
The ITN group showed greater improvement in AGI grade, abdominal circumference, and IAP (all P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed for MI, inflammatory markers, or severity scores (all P > 0.05). 28-day mortality and ICU length of stay did not differ significantly between groups. No ITN-related adverse events occurred. ITN may improve gastrointestinal parameters in sepsis-induced GID patients, but it did not significantly affect gastric motility, systemic inflammation, or global severity scores. Larger, controlled trials are needed to confirm its potential role as adjunctive therapy.
papers.title_ko: 패혈증 유발 위장관 기능장애에 대한 보조요법으로서의 피내 압정침 치료: 예비 무작위대조시험

summary.question: 패혈증 유발 위장관 기능장애 환자에서 피내 압정침 치료가 위장관 기능과 안전성에 도움이 되는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 중환자실의 패혈증 유발 위장관 기능장애 환자 60명을 일반치료군과 피내 압정침 추가군으로 무작위 배정한 예비 무작위대조시험이다.
summary.results: 피내 압정침군은 급성 위장관 손상 등급, 복부둘레, 복강내압이 더 개선되었고, 위운동성과 염증표지자, 중증도 점수, 28일 사망률과 ICU 재원기간은 차이가 없었으며 관련 이상반응도 없었다.

papers.title: Complementary and Integrative Health Approaches for Low Back Pain in Veterans: A Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Petri RP, Aoyagi K, Ibarra-Mejía G
papers.abstract:
Chronic low back pain (cLBP) is the most prevalent chronic pain condition among veterans, contributing to disability, reduced quality of life, and opioid dependence. Complementary and integrative health (CIH) approaches offer evidence-based, non-pharmacological alternatives that may improve pain management, enhance patient satisfaction, lower healthcare costs, and reduce opioid dependence.
The objective of the study was to synthesize current evidence on CIH approaches for veterans with cLBP, evaluate their impact on pain, function, and well-being, and identify implications for policy, health system implementation, and future research. The key questions of the study included: what is the effectiveness of CIH modalities in reducing cLBP intensity among veterans, what are their broader effects on health outcomes, opioid use, and quality of life, what barriers exist to implementation within the VA, and what research and policy priorities are needed to optimize veteran-centered CIH care? A narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2025 was conducted, prioritizing studies specific to veterans and incorporating systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and evidence maps. A patient-centered, biopsychosocial, and whole-health framework guided the analysis.
Evidence for CIH in veterans remains limited compared to that in civilian populations, but it demonstrates promise. Battlefield acupuncture demonstrated clinically meaningful reductions in pain, although yoga, Tai Chi, Qigong, and mindfulness offered modest improvements in pain and functional outcomes. Cognitive-behavioral therapy, Chiropractic care, and massage showed mixed results, with low to moderate certainty and limited durability. Multimodal approaches integrating CIH with conventional care have demonstrated the strongest outcomes, including reduced opioid prescriptions, improved coping, and potential cost savings. Barriers to care include provider shortages, administrative challenges, and uneven access across facilities.
CIH approaches represent patient-centered and holistic strategies with the potential to reduce pain, enhance function, and mitigate opioid reliance among veterans with cLBP. Broader, standardized implementation and veteran-specific trials are necessary to strengthen the evidence base and guide the sustainable integration of this approach into the VA health system.

papers.title: Acupuncture-antidepressant combinations for clinically diagnosed depressive disorders in China: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Qiu Q, Zhang Z, Yang W, Tew WY, Liu C, Leong Bin Abdullah MFI et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of acupuncture-antidepressant combinations for clinically diagnosed depressive disorders among participants recruited in China using a network meta-analysis.
PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to February 2025 for randomised controlled trials of acupuncture-antidepressant combinations and relevant pharmacological or acupuncture-related comparators. The principal efficacy outcome was change in Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD/HDRS) scores; safety outcomes included nausea/vomiting, dry mouth, headache, and treatment discontinuation. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Random-effects Bayesian network meta-analyses were conducted in R version 3.6.0 using gemtc version 0.8.1. Mean differences or odds ratios are presented with 95% credible intervals (CrIs), together with posterior rank-position probabilities. A standardised mean difference (SMD)-based sensitivity analysis assessed the influence of pooling HAMD-17 and HAMD-24.
Seventy-seven trials (7,031 participants) were included in the systematic review. Within the principal connected eight-node efficacy network, manual acupuncture plus selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors produced the largest reduction versus SSRI monotherapy (mean difference -3.37; 95% CrI -3.86 to -2.89) and the highest probability of occupying Rank 8 (the most effective position). Electroacupuncture plus SSRIs was also associated with a greater reduction in HAMD scores than SSRIs alone (MD -2.98; 95% CrI -3.66 to -2.31). Manual acupuncture plus SNRIs also favoured combination treatment (MD -3.16; 95% CrI -6.03 to -0.28), although the interval was comparatively wide. The SMD sensitivity analysis retained benefit for both EA + SSRIs and MA + SSRIs relative to SSRIs, although their relative ordering differed from the raw-MD analysis. The available adverse-event networks did not identify statistically clear differences from SSRI monotherapy; however, sparse events and very wide CrIs limit the strength of this finding.
Manual acupuncture plus an SSRI was associated with the largest short-term HAMD reduction in the primary raw-MD network. Relative treatment ordering differed in the SMD sensitivity analysis. The estimates should be interpreted cautiously because clinical heterogeneity, risk-of-bias concerns, sparse safety data, and limited follow-up preclude claims of equivalent safety or a preferred first-line strategy.

papers.title: Rhamnoside from Aquilaria sinensis leaves ameliorates chronic atrophic gastritis via immunomodulation and apoptosis regulation.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Yue B, Zhi Y, Lv N, Sun D, Wang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous inflammatory‑atrophic gastric disorder with limited effective therapies. Although Traditional Chinese medicine shows multi‑target benefits for CAG, the bioactivity of rare medicinal plant Aquilaria sinensis remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify anti‑inflammatory components from Aquilaria sinensis leaf extract and clarify the compound's anti‑CAG effects and mechanism.
Anti‑inflammatory constituents were screened. Macrophages stimulated by LPS and MNNG‑injured GES‑1 cells were used to assess cell viability, inflammation, cell‑cycle, proliferation and apoptosis. Transcriptomic‑proteomic profiling predicted candidate pathways. An MNNG‑combined rat CAG model was established; gross gastric observation, H&E, AB‑PAS, Masson staining, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry and qPCR were performed.
rhamnoside exhibited the strongest anti‑inflammatory activity. It reduced IL‑1β, IL‑6 and TNF‑α secretion and suppressed apoptosis in LPS‑treated macrophages, and triggered S‑phase cell‑cycle arrest in MNNG‑damaged GES‑1 cells. Omics analyses pinpointed PI3K/Akt as the core regulatory pathway. In vivo animal experiments demonstrated that rhamnoside dose‑dependently alleviated gastric gland atrophy, intestinal metaplasia and lamina propria fibrosis; it elevated PI3K/Akt signals, down‑regulated pro‑apoptotic BAX/caspase‑3, up‑regulated anti‑apoptotic BCL‑2, and normalized CAG‑associated gene transcription in gastric mucosa.
Rhamnoside from Aquilaria sinensis leaves protects against CAG by regulating immunity and inhibiting apoptosis via PI3K/Akt signaling, which provides a potential candidate for CAG experimental therapy.

papers.title: Interaction mechanisms of core dominant fungi during fermentation of Massa Medicata Fermentata: volatile compounds of Saccharomycopsis fibuligera inhibit the growth of Rhizopus oryzae.
papers.authors: Chang R, Liu J, Lian Y, Zhao J, Cao Q, Zhan X
papers.abstract: Massa Medicata Fermentata (MMF) is a traditional fermented medicine whose quality is governed by complex microbial interactions. This study investigated the antagonistic effect of the core yeast Saccharomycopsis fibuligera against the filamentous fungus Rhizopus oryzae and its underlying mechanisms. In vitro co-culture assays demonstrated that S. fibuligera suppressed R. oryzae growth and amylase activity in a cell-density-dependent manner, with significant inhibition observed at cell densities of ≥1 × 10⁷ cells·mL⁻¹. The antagonism was driven by two putative pathways: direct spatial/nutritional competition and indirect suppression mediated by yeast-secreted volatile organic compounds (VOCs). HS-SPME-GC-MS analysis identified six major VOCs, primarily fatty acid ethyl esters and 2-phenylethanol, with the latter being the most abundant (0.5664 ± 0.0422 µg·g⁻¹ medium). Single-compound antifungal assays confirmed that isoamyl acetate, ethyl hexanoate, and 2-phenylethanol completely inhibited the growth of R. oryzae at elevated doses. Mechanistic investigations via SEM, PI staining, and biochemical assays revealed that these VOCs induce cell death by disrupting mycelial morphology, compromising membrane integrity, inhibiting ergosterol biosynthesis, and triggering lipid peroxidation. These findings elucidate a key antagonistic interaction between core functional fungi during MMF fermentation, providing a theoretical basis for targeted fermentation regulation and industrial standardization of this traditional herbal medicine.IMPORTANCEBy revealing the cell-density-dependent dual-mode antagonism between S. fibuligera and R. oryzae, this study deepens our understanding of microbial interactions in traditional fermentation. The discovery of specific inhibitory VOCs and their membrane-disrupting mechanisms provides a theoretical basis for targeted process regulation. These insights are crucial for achieving precise fermentation control, which is essential for improving product consistency, reducing batch-to-batch variability, and advancing the traditional fermentation standardization of herbal medicines.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture exerts an analgesic effect by inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation in the periaqueductal gray in a rat model of bone cancer pain.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Li X, Wu S, Zhang X, Xie S, Wang W, You X et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) at ST36 and BL60 in a rat model of bone cancer pain (BCP) to provide a theoretical basis and guidance for the clinical treatment of BCP.
In experiment 1, rats were assigned to sham, untreated model (BCP), EA-treated model (BCP + EA) and sham EA-treated model (BCP + SEA) groups. Pain was assessed behaviorally by a paw withdrawal threshold and limb use score. The activation of microglia and astrocytes in the periaqueductal gray was detected by immunohistochemistry. Expression of nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3), caspase-1 and interleukin (IL)-1β in the periaqueductal gray matter was detected by Western blotting. A NLRP3 agonist (nigericin sodium salt (NSS)) was used in experiment 2, wherein rats were assigned to sham, BCP, BCP + EA and BCP + EA + NSS groups. For the overexpression of NLRP3, rats in the BCP + EA + NSSgroup were injected intraperitoneally with NSS on day 17 after surgery.
EA markedly relieved BCP and suppressed the overexpression of NLRP3/caspase-1/IL-1β in the periaqueductal gray, which is related to the activation of astrocytes and microglial cells. Pharmacological activation of NLRP3 reversed the analgesic effect of EA and increased the expression of NLRP3/caspase-1/IL-1β in the periaqueductal gray. In addition, c-fos was significantly downregulated by EA and this effect was also reversed by the NLRP3 agonist, suggesting that the role of EA in BCP may involve mitigation of inflammation.
EA interferes with the NLRP3/caspase-1/IL-1β pathway in the periaqueductal gray to exert an analgesic effect in this rat model of BCP.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture regulates colonic motility in a rat model of stress.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Zhao YX, Xin JJ, Zhang WX, Zhou YX
papers.abstract:
It is well established that endogenous and exogenous corticotrophin-releasing factor (CRF) stimulates colonic motility in rodents. Electroacupuncture (EA) has shown promise in relieving stress responses and alleviating colonic dysmotility, but less is known about its underlying mechanism of action in this context. This study was designed to elucidate the effects of EA on colorectal dysfunction in a rat model of stress and to clarify the underlying mechanism.
A rat model of stress was induced using exogenous CRF. Colonic propulsion was evaluated by the bead latency test, and colorectal motility was recorded in vivo by implanting a manometric capsule into the colorectal lumen. To clarify the role of CRF receptors type 1 and 2 on stress-induced colonic dysfunction, corresponding selective antagonists (CP-154526 and Astressin 2B, respectively) were administered accordingly. Western blot analysis was used to detect protein expression of CRF and its receptors in the hypothalamus and colorectum.
CRF-induced stress significantly accelerated colonic motility. EA treatment alleviated colonic motor dysfunction and reduced colonic propulsion. CP-154526, but not Astressin 2B, reversed CRF-induced colonic dysmotility, suggesting an essential role of CRF receptor type 1 in stress-induced colonic motor disorders. EA treatment resulted in an inhibition of the protein overexpression of CRF receptor type 1 in both the hypothalamus and colorectum in this rat model of stress.
EA ameliorated stress-induced colonic dysmotility, most likely through regulation of central and peripheral expression of CRF receptor type 1.

papers.title: Multi-target network modulation of Traditional Chinese Medicine in radiation enteropathy: mechanistic insights and therapeutic implications.
papers.authors: Tan B, Chen X, Shao G, Su H, Ma X, Ni X et al.
papers.abstract: Radiation enteropathy (RE) is a common and clinically significant complication of abdominal and pelvic radiotherapy, characterized by multifactorial pathological processes including oxidative DNA damage, epithelial barrier disruption, immune-inflammatory dysregulation, vascular injury, fibrosis, and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Despite its clinical burden, effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), widely used in the management of gastrointestinal disorders, has attracted increasing attention as a complementary approach for radiation-induced intestinal injury. Accumulating experimental evidence indicates that TCM formulas, herbal extracts, and bioactive phytochemicals may exert protective effects through coordinated regulation of interconnected pathological processes. Reported protective effects involve several interconnected pathological processes, but the supporting evidence remains uneven. Most studies use acute, single-dose animal models, and many mechanistic conclusions rely on pathway-marker changes rather than functional perturbation. This review therefore evaluates TCM interventions according to disease stage, intestinal site, irradiation design, and the strength of mechanistic support. Multi-target regulation is treated as an interpretive framework rather than a mechanism established for every intervention. Clinical evidence remains limited by small samples, heterogeneous preparations, inconsistent endpoints, and inadequate follow-up. Translation will require standardized products, clinically relevant fractionated and tumor-bearing models, exposure-relevant mechanistic validation, and rigorous trials that assess intestinal benefit without compromising tumor control.

papers.title: Phenolic constituents from Rhododendron anthopogonoides and their bioactivities.
papers.authors: Zong WY, Wang JX, Huang LX, Han YJ, Cheng GG, Yu MY et al.
papers.abstract: Rhododendron anthopogonoides, an important medicinal plant, has been historically used in both traditional Chinese medicine and Tibetan folk medicine. The first phytochemical investigation on the water-soluble fraction of its leaves and twigs led to the isolation of seven new aromatic glycosides, named anthopogosides A-G (1-7), together with 15 known compounds (8-22). Their chemical structures and absolute configurations were unambiguously elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analysis (NMR and HRMS) and quantum chemical calculations (NMR and ECD). Compounds 3-5, 15, 16, and 21 showed significant anti-inflammatory activity at the concentration of 40 μM. Compound 10 exhibited the most potent DPPH and ABTS free radical scavenging capacities with IC50 values 29.46 ± 0.07 and 79.10 ± 1.07 μM, respectively. In addition, flavonoid trimers 20 and 22 displayed outstanding α-glucosidase inhibitory activity with IC50 values of 0.48 ± 0.02 and 0.47 ± 0.02 μM, which were 700-fold higher than that of the positive control acarbose. These findings could greatly enrich the chemical diversity of water-soluble constituents from Rhododendron species and highlighted their potential applications.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Traditional Chinese Medicine Exercise Therapy for Frailty in Older Adults and Descriptive Summary of Exercise Prescription Characteristics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
papers.authors: Huang X, Xin B, Wang R, Cui J, Li M, Jiang W et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate outcome-specific effects of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) exercise therapy on frailty-related outcomes in older adults and descriptively summarize exercise prescription characteristics.
Systematic review and meta-analysis.
Randomized controlled trials involving adults aged 60 years or older with frailty, prefrailty, or eligible cognitive frailty in community, institutional, or clinical settings.
Eight databases were searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias. Separate random-effects meta-analyses were conducted for key outcomes using standardized mean differences (SMDs) with Hedges' g correction. Heterogeneity was assessed using τ2 and I2 statistics, with prediction intervals calculated where appropriate. Exercise prescription characteristics were summarized descriptively.
Twenty-one studies were included, with 15 contributing to the main meta-analysis. TCM exercise therapy showed favorable effects on Edmonton Frail Scale scores (SMD, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.04-1.06), Fried frailty phenotype scores (SMD, 2.70; 95% CI, 1.15-4.25), Timed Up and Go performance (SMD, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.17-1.33), Berg Balance Scale scores (SMD, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.00-1.64), and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores (SMD, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.63-1.41). Gait speed was not significantly improved, and grip strength showed a small, imprecise effect. Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes. Tai Chi and Baduanjin were the most frequently represented modalities, whereas reported exercise prescription characteristics varied across studies.
TCM exercise therapy may benefit selected frailty, mobility, balance, and cognitive outcomes, but heterogeneity and limited evidence for several outcomes warrant caution. Exercise prescription characteristics are descriptive and hypothesis generating, not evidence for an optimized frequency, intensity, time, type, volume, and progression prescription.

papers.title: Efficacy of Electroacupuncture Compared With Topical Diclofenac Sodium Gel for Patients With Hand Osteoarthritis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Wang W, Kang J, Shi J, Jiao R, Zang Z, Long Z et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of 4-week electroacupuncture (EA) compared with topical diclofenac sodium gel (DSG) for hand osteoarthritis (HOA).
Participants with symptomatic HOA for at least 3 months were randomly assigned to receive either 12 sessions of EA or topical DSG at a dose of 2 g 4 times per day for 4 weeks followed by a 12-week follow-up. The primary outcome was the change in the average overall finger joint pain intensity in the dominant hand during the previous 48 hours measured on the visual analog scale (0, no pain; 100, maximal pain) from baseline at week 4. The research period was from September 1, 2020, to March 17, 2024, and the statistical analyses were completed by March 15, 2025.
A total of 120 (n=60 in each group) participants were included. The overall finger joint pain intensity measured with the visual analog scale in the dominant hand during the previous 48 hours at week 4 was 28.72 (95% CI, 24.21 to 33.23) in the EA group and 42.82 (95% CI, 38.32 to 47.33) in the DSG group (between-group difference, -14.11; 95% CI, -20.49 to -7.73; P<.001). Similar between-group differences favoring EA were observed at week 8 and week 16. Treatment-related adverse events were rare, relatively mild, and transient in the trial.
Treatment of HOA with EA for 4 weeks had clinically meaningful effects on reducing pain compared with topical DSG, and the effects persisted through the 12-week follow-up. Electroacupuncture may be considered a promising nonpharmacologic therapy for HOA.

papers.title: Adjunctive effects of acupuncture and moxibustion in women with premature ovarian insufficiency receiving hormone replacement therapy: protocol for a multicenter, assessor-blinded, 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Lu C, Ye T, Cui J, Chen B
papers.abstract:
Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is characterized by impaired ovarian function before 40 years of age and is associated with menstrual disturbance, infertility, hypoestrogenic symptoms, psychological distress, and long-term health risks. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is recommended for symptom control and prevention of estrogen-deficiency-related complications but does not reliably restore ovarian activity or fertility potential. Acupuncture and moxibustion are used as complementary interventions for ovarian dysfunction; however, evidence regarding their independent and combined adjunctive effects in women with POI remains limited.
This prospective, multicenter, assessor-blinded, 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial will recruit 144 women with POI from three clinical centers. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to estradiol/dydrogesterone alone, acupuncture plus estradiol/dydrogesterone, moxibustion plus estradiol/dydrogesterone, or combined acupuncture and moxibustion plus estradiol/dydrogesterone. The intervention period will last 12 weeks. The primary outcome is the change from baseline to week 12 in antral follicle count (AFC). Secondary outcomes include serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), sex hormones, ovarian hemodynamic parameters, menopausal and anxiety symptoms, Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome scores, and menstrual status. Clinical pregnancy will be analyzed as an exploratory reproductive outcome during treatment and follow-up at weeks 24 and 48. Factorial models will estimate the main effects of acupuncture and moxibustion, whereas the acupuncture × moxibustion interaction will be considered exploratory.
This trial will evaluate the adjunctive effects of acupuncture and moxibustion on AFC and related secondary clinical outcomes in a selected subgroup of women with POI receiving standard HRT. The factorial design will permit estimation of the independent effects of both interventions and exploratory assessment of their potential interaction.

papers.title: Narrative review of non-pharmacological interventions for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: exercise, physical therapy, cryotherapy and acupuncture.
papers.authors: Li L, Fan M, Ni L, Wang J, Qiao L
papers.abstract:
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a heterogeneous, treatment-limiting adverse event of cytotoxic chemotherapy that impairs sensory, motor, autonomic and balance function, and substantially reduces cancer patients' quality of life. Current pharmacotherapy options are limited: duloxetine is the only guideline-recommended agent for established painful CIPN, while no drugs are approved for primary prevention. Non-pharmacological interventions have emerged as promising adjunctive strategies, yet evidence strength varies widely across modalities and patient subgroups. This narrative review aimed to synthesize contemporary clinical evidence of non-pharmacological interventions for CIPN prevention, symptom treatment and functional rehabilitation, to deliver stratified, chemotherapy-specific clinical guidance and identify gaps for future research.
A narrative review design was adopted, without pre-registration or standardized systematic review screening protocols. Targeted manual literature retrieval was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI and Wanfang Data for peer-reviewed human clinical studies published between January 2018 and March 2025. We focused on four core non-pharmacological modalities for CIPN: multimodal exercise therapy, physical therapy incorporating cryotherapy, acupuncture-based complementary therapies, and behavioral self-management interventions. High-certainty evidence was defined as consistent results from large multicenter randomized controlled trials and network meta-analyses; moderate/low-certainty evidence was derived from small single-center trials and observational studies.
Cumulative stratified evidence demonstrates clear heterogeneity in intervention efficacy and clinical applicability. Multimodal supervised exercise and physical rehabilitation carry the most consistent high-certainty evidence for both primary CIPN prevention and functional recovery, with significant improvements in numbness, neuropathic pain, balance and muscle strength. Cryotherapy shows robust preventive efficacy exclusively in patients receiving taxane chemotherapy, with insufficient supportive data for platinum or vinca alkaloid regimens. Acupuncture, including warm needle acupuncture, TEAS and electroacupuncture, provides moderate-to-low certainty adjunctive relief for refractory established CIPN symptoms but is not recommended as first-line therapy. Behavioral interventions exert limited direct therapeutic effects on nerve injury, yet effectively improve symptom coping, treatment adherence and long-term self-management. All interventions exhibit favorable safety profiles with minimal severe adverse events when individualized to patient fitness, comorbidities and chemotherapy regimens.
Non-pharmacological interventions cannot be considered uniformly effective for all CIPN populations; evidence strength and clinical indications differ markedly by modality. Supervised multimodal exercise and physical rehabilitation represent first-line adjunctive strategies for broad CIPN prevention and functional recovery. Cryotherapy is a targeted preventive option limited to taxane-treated patients. Acupuncture serves as secondary adjunctive care for persistent symptoms, while behavioral interventions function as supportive self-management tools. Clinical implementation requires agent-specific patient stratification, individualized intervention prescription, standardized validated CIPN assessment tools, and integrated multidisciplinary oncology rehabilitation pathways. Further large, stratified randomized controlled trials with long-term follow-up are required to standardize intervention protocols and validate sustained clinical benefits.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics, network pharmacology, and machine learning reveal the active constituents and pharmacological mechanism of Fufang E'jiao Jiang against lung cancer-related fatigue.
papers.authors: Shen K, Sun H, Yang L, Feng Q, Zhang N, Zhao C et al.
papers.abstract: Fufang E'jiao Jiang (FEJ), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula for improving immunity, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in alleviating lung cancer-related fatigue (LCRF). FEJ contains both plant-derived herbs and animal-derived donkey-hide gelatin, yet its complex chemical composition-particularly the collagen-derived peptides and proteins-remains incompletely characterized. However, a systematic characterization of its complex chemical composition remains lacking, and the underlying anti-LCRF mechanism of its are yet to be fully elucidated. By integrating metabolomics (UHPLC-QTOF-MS and GC-MS), peptidomics, and proteomics (NanoLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS), we identified 186 small molecules, 243 peptides, and 42 proteins in FEJ, substantially expanding the chemical coverage relative to previous reports that focused mainly on small molecules. Notably, collagen-derived peptides and proteins from donkey-hide gelatin were characterized for the first time. Network pharmacology and consensus machine learning (LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE) prioritized 17 potential key constituents (including 8 donkey-hide gelatin peptides, 5 ginsenosides, and others), spanning all five constituent medicinal materials. Six core targets (IL1B, IL6, TNF, MTOR, BCL2L1, and BDNF) were screened and were predicted to be associated with the regulation of inflammation, energy metabolism, and skeletal muscle function, potentially through the NF-κB and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways. The main novelty lies in the first comprehensive characterization of FEJ including peptides and proteins, and in the establishment of a multi-omics workflow applicable to animal-containing traditional Chinese medicine formulas. These findings provide a solid chemical basis for deciphering the anti-LCRF mechanisms of FEJ and warrant further experimental validation.

papers.title: Acupuncture for relief of gagging in patients undergoing transoesophageal echocardiography-a randomised placebo-controlled trial.
papers.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
papers.authors: Usichenko TI, Müller-Kozarez I, Busch R, Knigge S, Busch M
papers.abstract:
Gagging during transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) can make the procedure distressing and even impossible to perform. Acupuncture is suggested to relieve the gag reflex during peroral endoscopic procedures. The aim was to test whether acupuncture is better than placebo for reducing gagging in patients undergoing elective ambulatory TEE.
Sixty patients scheduled for ambulatory TEE were included according to eligibility criteria and received either fixed intradermal needles (N = 30) or placebo needles at acupuncture points CV24 and PC6 in a random order prior to TEE. Patients and practitioners, who performed TEE procedure and assessed the outcome measures were unaware of group (acupuncture or placebo) allocation. The primary outcome was the intensity of gagging, measured using verbal rating scale (VRS-11). Secondary outcomes included the use of rescue medication, the incidence of gagging, patients' satisfaction with relief of unwanted side effects during TEE procedure, success of patients' blinding, heart rate and oxygen saturation.
Median (IQR) of patient's reported gagging intensity in the acupuncture group was 4 (2-8) vs. 7 (5-8) in the placebo group (P = 0.13), the gagging intensity reported by TEE-examiner was 2 (1-5) among the patients from the acupuncture group vs. 4 (2-9) in the placebo group (P = 0.06). Six patients from the acupuncture group vs. 14 from the placebo group required sedative rescue medication (P = 0.03). All other measured outcomes were comparable between the study groups.
Acupuncture with indwelling fixed intradermal needles may reduce the need for sedative medication in patients scheduled for elective TEE. Larger trials with improved methodology are required to verify this finding.
NCT03821428; registration date: January 25, 2019.

papers.title: Qi-Blood Harmony Formula mediates post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis: a multi-omics validation.
papers.authors: Xie X, Wang Y, Dong X, Yuan R, Miao Y, Li P et al.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Persistent myocardial fibrosis and dysregulated energy metabolism following MI contribute to adverse cardiac remodeling and are associated with poor clinical prognosis. Currently, no guideline-recommended therapy provides effective long-term intervention simultaneously targeting both of these core pathological mechanisms. The Qi-Blood Harmony Formula (QBHF), a classical Chinese herbal prescription, has demonstrated cardioprotective potential on attenuating fibrosis, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and restoring myocardial ATP levels in MI, yet its underlying mechanisms and therapeutic targets remain unclear. Using an integrated multi-omics approach in a mouse MI model, we showed that QBHF reactivated genes related to energy metabolism while suppressing pro-fibrotic pathways, as revealed by bulk RNA-sequencing. Non-targeted metabolomics further confirmed its efficacy in counteracting metabolic dysregulation. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that QBHF altered cardiac cellular composition characterized by reducing a major profibrotic fibroblast subpopulation and expanding a metabolically robust cardiomyocyte subset. Integrative multi-omics analysis identified the fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) as a central regulatory hub modulated by QBHF across bulk heart tissue, fibroblasts, and cardiomyocytes. Crucially, heterozygous knockout of FTO in mice abolished QBHF-mediated improvements in cardiac fibrosis, ATP level and heart function. Consistently, FTO knockdown in cardiomyocytes blunted QBHF-induced ATP restoration. Together, these findings demonstrate that QBHF confers post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis. Our findings highlight FTO as a promising therapeutic target and provide novel mechanistic insights into traditional Chinese medicine-based interventions for post-MI injury.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic, molecular dynamic simulation and in vitro analysis identify Evodiamine as a multi-target therapeutic agent against cisplatin-resistant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Patra SK, Rajeshwari R, Barik K, Kumar A, Biswal BK
papers.abstract:
An integrative transcriptomic, computational, and experimental approach was employed to identify molecular determinants of cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and to investigate the therapeutic potential of Evodiamine (Evo). Analysis of multiple Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets identified 100 overlapping differentially expressed genes, followed by protein-protein interaction network analysis that prioritized SPP1, GPX3, HBEGF, and KLF2 as key hub genes. Expression analysis demonstrated significantly increased SPP1 and reduced GPX3 and KLF2 expression in NSCLC tissues, while survival analysis revealed an association between elevated SPP1 expression and poor overall survival. Gene Ontology and KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that the identified hub genes were predominantly associated with extracellular matrix organization, ErbB signaling, glutathione metabolism, and apelin signaling. Molecular docking analysis demonstrated favourable binding of Evo to the identified hub proteins, with SPP1, GPX3, HBEGF, and KLF2 showing docking scores of -9.1, -8.9, -8.9, and - 8.5 kcal/mol, respectively. Subsequently, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable SPP1-Evo interactions throughout the simulation period. In vitro validation further demonstrated that Evo significantly reduced cell viability (A549: IC50 = 4 ± 0.23 µM, A549CR: IC50 = 2 ± 0.31 µM), clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in both cisplatin-sensitive and cisplatin-resistant NSCLC (A549, A549CR) cells. Interestingly, Evo showed better sensitivity towards A549CR cells than parental A549. Evo treatment also increased intracellular reactive oxygen species generation, mitochondrial membrane depolarization, DNA damage, and apoptotic cell death. Furthermore, Evo modulated the expression of the identified hub genes in NSCLC cells, supporting their potential involvement in its anticancer activity. Collectively, the integrated bioinformatics, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and experimental findings identify SPP1, GPX3, HBEGF, and KLF2 as potential molecular regulators associated with cisplatin resistance and demonstrate the multi-target anticancer activity of Evo against cisplatin-sensitive and cisplatin-resistant NSCLC, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for overcoming cisplatin resistance.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05107-0.

papers.title: Warm needle acupuncture at Jiaji points for lumbar disc herniation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
papers.authors: Zuo R, Yun J, Lin X, He X, Qiu F
papers.abstract: BackgroundWarm needle acupuncture (WNA) has been widely used in the treatment of lumbar disc herniation (LDH). However, variations in acupoint selection across studies may influence the evaluation of its efficacy. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of WNA at Jiaji points compared with conventional acupuncture for LDH.MethodsA systematic search was conducted in the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, PubMed, EMBASE, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP databases from inception to March 17, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing WNA at Jiaji points with conventional acupuncture were included. Primary outcomes were total effective rate, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score, and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to explore heterogeneity and assess robustness, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.ResultsA total of 27 RCTs involving 2266 participants were included. Meta-analysis showed that WNA significantly improved the total effective rate compared with conventional acupuncture (RR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.21-1.31, P < 0.00001). In addition, WNA significantly reduced VAS scores (MD = -1.39, 95% CI: -1.72 to -1.06, P < 0.00001) and ODI scores (MD = -5.24, 95% CI: -6.23 to -4.25, P < 0.00001). However, substantial heterogeneity was observed for VAS and ODI, and sensitivity analyses did not fully explain the residual heterogeneity. The certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low.ConclusionsWNA at Jiaji points may improve pain, functional disability, and overall clinical response compared with conventional acupuncture in patients with LDH. However, methodological limitations, substantial heterogeneity, and low to very low certainty of evidence limit confidence in the magnitude of the pooled effects. Further rigorously designed, adequately powered multicenter RCTs are needed.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Traditional Chinese Fitness Methods on Depressive Symptoms and Glycaemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Comorbid Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Taijiquan and Baduanjin.
papers.authors: Tian X, Wei Y, Bo J, Lin K, Shen Y, Liu Y
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the overall effectiveness of traditional Chinese fitness methods (TCFMs)-specifically Taijiquan and Baduanjin-on depressive symptoms and glycaemic control in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and comorbid depression.
RCTs evaluating the effectiveness of TCFMs were identified through 10 major English and Chinese databases, including PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, ProQuest, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by intervention duration, frequency, and sample size.
Eight RCTs of Taijiquan and Baduanjin were included. All studies were conducted in China, and most had small sample sizes. Most had a high risk of bias, mainly due to a lack of blinding of participants and personnel. TCFMs were associated with significant improvements in depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.39, 95% CI [-2.22, -0.57], p = 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed for HbA1c (MD = -0.82, 95% CI [-1.18, -0.45], p < 0.0001) and FPG (MD = -0.70, 95% CI [-0.97, -0.42], p < 0.00001). The effect on 2hPBG remains inconclusive owing to limited studies. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant effect modifiers for depressive symptoms or HbA1c (all interaction p > 0.05). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary findings, though heterogeneity decreased substantially after excluding high-risk studies.
This review provides preliminary evidence that TCFMs may confer benefits on mental health and glycaemic regulation in patients with T2DM and comorbid depression. However, given the low certainty of the evidence, high heterogeneity, and methodological limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. The conclusions are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, rigorously designed studies.
The protocol of this systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261287519).

papers.authors: Lan G, Wu M, Zhang J, Li Y, Wang Y, Su Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To characterize the methodological quality, certainty of evidence, primary-study overlap, outcome coverage, and recurrent acupuncture prescription patterns in the existing secondary evidence on acupuncture for poststroke dysphagia (PSD).
Systematic reviews and meta-analyses (SRs/MAs) evaluating acupuncture for PSD were identified. Methodological quality was assessed using A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, and primary-study overlap using the corrected covered area (CCA). Evidence mapping summarized outcome coverage and certainty, and prescription pattern mining explored frequently used acupoints and combinations.
Forty-five SRs/MAs were included. Under the original AMSTAR 2 critical-domain configuration, one review was rated moderate, eight low, and 36 critically low. GRADE indicated that most outcome evidence was of low or very low certainty. The CCA was 0.34%, indicating slight overlap of primary studies across reviews. Evidence was concentrated on total effective rate and swallowing-function outcomes, whereas patient-important outcomes, including aspiration/pneumonia, nutritional status, safety, and quality of life, were underrepresented. Frequently used acupoints included Fengchi (GB20), Lianquan (RN23), Jinjin (EX-HN12), and Yuye (EX-HN13), with recurrent combinations reflecting local stimulation and swallowing-related functional regulation.
Current secondary evidence suggests that acupuncture, primarily as an adjunctive intervention, may improve swallowing-related outcomes in PSD, but confidence remains limited by methodological weaknesses and low certainty of evidence. Future studies should improve methodological rigor, standardize clinically important outcomes, and prospectively validate recurrent prescription patterns.

papers.title: LIPUS promotes calcium oscillations to improve lymphatic drainage and alleviates cold-stimulated pain and effusion in osteoarthritis joints.
papers.authors: Yang J, Liu R, Yang X, Li X, Peng X, Han J et al.
papers.abstract:
Osteoarthritis (OA) patients in remission usually experience acute exacerbations of pain and joint swelling following cold stimulation. This represents one of the characteristic clinical presentations of "cold knees". In Traditional Chinese Medicine, this phenomenon correlates with "Cold Bi", reflecting "lingering dampness" and "stagnation of Blood and Qi" in the joints, and is conceptually consistent with dysfunction of synovial lymphatic system (SLS) observed in OA. However, the underlying mechanisms of cold-exacerbated OA and the therapeutic strategies remain poorly explored.
OA mouse models were established by destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) surgery. The mice were exposed to cold stimulation at 4 weeks post-surgery to mimic OA patients in remission experiencing acute cold stimulation. Joint pain-related behaviors were assessed using multiple approaches including gait analysis and von Frey test. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) was used to evaluate joint effusion. Near-infrared indocyanine green (NIR-ICG) imaging and intra-articular injections of Fluorescein isothiocyanate-dextran (FITC-dextran) were employed to assess lymphatic drainage. Furthermore, the effects of temperature decrease and low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) on calcium oscillations and nitric oxide (NO) production by lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) were investigated using live-cell fluorescence imaging. Additionally, the mechanisms through which LIPUS plays therapeutic roles were also explored using transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) inhibitor HC-067047.
Acute cold stimulation aggravated gait abnormality and decreased paw withdrawal threshold in DMM-operated mice. Furthermore, weight-bearing asymmetry and total locomotor distance in the open field were also worsened in these mice. The knee joint effusion was significantly aggravated following acute cold stimulation accompanied by impaired synovial lymphatic drainage. Mechanistically, cold stimulation suppressed calcium oscillations of LECs and decreased their NO production, which were efficiently restored by LIPUS. Additionally, LIPUS treatment improved lymphatic drainage of the knee joint and alleviated cold-stimulated exacerbation of OA phenotypes in mice. These therapeutic effects were significantly suppressed under TRPV4 inhibition as well as hindlimb lymphatic vessel ligation.
Dysfunction of lymphatic drainage contributes to cold-stimulated exacerbation of OA phenotypes in mice, which could be alleviated by LIPUS-induced NO production through the TRPV4/Ca2+/eNOS/NO axis. These findings provide novel insights into the mechanisms of "cold knees" and highlight the therapeutic potential of LIPUS in the treatment of pain and joint effusion in OA.The translational potential of this article: Our study suggests that LIPUS ameliorates cold-induced worsening of pain and joint effusion in OA by improving synovial lymphatic drainage. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the translational potential of LIPUS application in skeletal disorders characterized by lymphatic drainage dysfunction.

papers.title: Shexiang Huayu Xingnao Granule Alleviates Intracerebral Hemorrhage via PI3K/AKT-Mediated Neuroinflammation Regulation: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
papers.authors: RuKui Y, MingLi W, Chun L, MeiJuan C, Yuan Y
papers.abstract:
Employing network pharmacology prediction combined with experimental validation, this research elucidated the underlying mechanisms of Shexiang Huayu Xingnao granules (SXHY) against intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).
Potential targets and related signaling pathways of SXHY acting on ICH were predicted through network pharmacology. An autologous blood injection-induced rat ICH model was established, with simvastatin as the positive control drug. The therapeutic effects of SXHY were evaluated using neurological function scores, brain water content, superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, malondialdehyde activity, and brain tissue hemorrhage area. Mechanism studies used a lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV-2 microglial cell model, assessing inflammatory mediator expression profiles and PI3K/AKT pathway modulation through RT-qPCR and Western blot analysis.
Network pharmacology analysis revealed 360 common SXHY-ICH targets, with 10 core targets (including TNF, AKT1, IL-6, and IL-1β) significantly enriched in the PI3K/AKT, AGE-RAGE, and MAPK pathways; molecular docking further demonstrated potent binding of the key component stigmasterol to TNF-α (binding energy: -9.125 kcal/mol) and IL-6 (binding energy: -8.57 kcal/mol). Animal experiments showed within-group improvements in neurological function from day 2 to day 3 post-ICH in SXHY groups. The observed proportions of animals with improved neurological scores were 88.9% (low-dose), 83.3% (high-dose), 70.0% (model), and 62.5% (simvastatin). However, no statistically significant between-group differences were observed at day 3 (p > 0.05). It also reduced brain edema (high dose: 78.0 ± 0.7% vs.
80.5 ± 1.0%, p < 0.01) and significantly decreased hematoma area (high dose: 0.35 ± 0.50 mm2 vs. model: 1.02 ± 0.93 mm2, p < 0.05); meanwhile, it significantly increased SOD activity (high dose: 68.7 ± 11.3 U/mg protein vs. model: 37.3±14.1 U/mg protein, p < 0.01). Cell experiments further confirmed that SXHY mediates anti-inflammatory activity through modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling, including reduced p-PI3K/GAPDH (p < 0.01), downregulation of proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α/IL-6/IL-1β mRNA (p < 0.01), and upregulation of anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 mRNA (p < 0.05).
SXHY may alleviate post-ICH brain injury by inhibiting neuroinflammation throu modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway. The results provide new mechanistic evidence for traditional Chinese medicine interventions against ICH.

papers.title: Advancements in Natural Product-Based Ischemic Stroke Treatment: Mechanisms, Key Compounds, and Drug Delivery Systems.
papers.authors: Yang N, Li M, Wang M, Li X, Dong H, Yao J et al.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains the leading global cause of permanent neurological disability and mortality. Narrow therapeutic time windows and elevated hemorrhagic transformation risks restrict conventional clinical interventions, including intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. Single-target neuroprotective agents fail to sustain long-term neurological functional recovery, resulting in unsatisfactory clinical outcomes. Natural products (NPs) derived from traditional Chinese medicine exert protective effects against cerebral ischemia via multiple pathways. However, their poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, low aqueous solubility, and inadequate in vivo bioavailability greatly hinder clinical translational application. This review systematically summarizes the pathological mechanisms of natural monomers for the treatment of ischemic stroke and four types of brain-targeted nanocarriers over the past decade. We reconstructed the pathological cascades of cerebral ischemia across the acute, subacute, and chronic repair phases, and critically discussed the inherent limitations of the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model and existing monomer-based preclinical studies. This work provides systematic structure-activity relationship evidence and insights into nano-delivery strategies for the development of natural product-based anti-stroke therapeutics. We also propose future research directions, such as staged, sequential administration, precise multi-omics intervention, and standardized nanoformulation development, to accelerate the clinical translation of bioactive ingredients derived from traditional Chinese medicine.
